title: Twenty Three: Build It, Trade It, Grow It

curriculum.resolved: A focused primary whole-number place-value demonstration; no syllabus certification

objectives.text: Identify a digit’s value from its hundreds, tens or ones position.

prerequisites: Count to ten and read three-digit whole numbers.
Recognize multiplication by ten as ten equal copies.

concept.hook: Can the same cubes tell us what a digit means?
concept.analogy: Physical base-ten cubes, rods and flats represent their actual quantities.
concept.arc: Build twenty three, regroup without changing its total, connect blocks to digits, then contrast multiplication by ten and practise.

scenes.title: Can you see twenty three?
scenes.narration: Look at these twenty three cubes. Gather them into groups of ten, with three left over. Read the number: two tens and three ones make twenty three.

cues.phrase: Look at these twenty three cubes
Gather them into groups of ten

scenes.title: Trade, without changing the total
scenes.narration: Start with one ten and thirteen ones. Trade ten of those ones for another ten. Count the result: two tens and three ones. We still have twenty three!

visual.label: A trade keeps the same quantity

scenes.title: The place gives the value
scenes.narration: See our two tens and three ones. Separate their values: the tens are worth twenty, and the ones are worth three. Write twenty plus three: twenty three.

scenes.title: Now make it ten times as much
scenes.narration: Begin with twenty three again. Multiply the whole quantity by ten: each digit moves one place left. Read two hundred and thirty. Our three ones have become three tens, worth thirty.

visual.label: Multiplying by ten changes the quantity

cues.phrase: Multiply the whole quantity by ten

scenes.title: Same total, or a bigger total?
scenes.narration: Here are two hundreds and three tens. Notice the empty ones column. Write zero there: our model has no loose ones. Trading kept twenty three unchanged; multiplying made it ten times as much.

scenes.title: Your turn
scenes.narration: In three hundred and forty, what is the value of the digit four? Think about its place.

items: Find the value of four in 340.
visual.label: Think before the answer

scenes.title: Four tens are forty
scenes.narration: Build three hundred and forty with three hundreds and four tens. Separate the tens: four groups of ten. Write their value, forty. The digit four is worth forty because it is in the tens place.

scenes.title: Find the place. Find the value.
scenes.narration: Return to our model of twenty three. Separate the tens from the ones. Read the values: two means twenty here, and three means three. Find the place to find the value!

visual.label: Place tells us the digit’s value

cues.phrase: Return to our model of twenty three
Separate the tens from the ones
